findings.summary: Subdomain allowance feature is completely broken: the allowSubdomains check at lines 461-467 is unreachable dead code because every code path in the preceding if/else block (lines 415-459) returns, making allowSubdomains always ignored regardless of configuration
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a crawl with allowSubdomains=true for example.com. When crawling discovers blog.example.com/page, isInternalLink returns false (different hostnames), the external block runs, and since allowExternalContentLinks defaults to false, the link is denied as EXTERNAL_LINK at line 458 — execution never reaches the subdomain check at line 461 that would have allowed it. Users depending on subdomain crawling will silently miss all subdomain content.

findings.summary: Missing denialReasons entries for URL parse errors in filterLinks: two return-false paths (lines 145-152 and 202-208) don't call denialReasons.set(), leaving the denial reasons Map incomplete for parse-failed URLs
findings.failure_scenario: filterLinks is called with a URL that causes new URL(link.trim(), this.baseUrl) to throw at line 144. The URL is denied (return false at line 151) but denialReasons never records it. At queue-worker.ts line 1450, denialReasons.get(url) returns undefined for such a URL, and the consumer falls back to a generic message like 'Source URL is not allowed by crawl configuration' rather than the accurate DenialReason.URL_PARSE_ERROR, producing misleading error messages.
